arabic_blocks: [699] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أنس بن مالك الأنصارى أن رسول الله ﷺ ركب فرسا فجحش شقه الأيمن قال أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه فصلى لنا يومئذ صلاة من الصلوات وهو قاعد فصلينا وراءه قعودا، ثم قال لما سلم إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا صلى قائما فصلوا قياما وإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا رفع فارفعوا وإذا سجد فاسجدوا وإذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده فقولوا ربنا ولك الحمد
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari informed me:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode a horse and his right side was grazed. Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: That day he led us in one of the prayers while seated, and we prayed seated behind him. Then, after he gave the greeting of peace, he said, “The imam has only been appointed to be followed. When he prays standing, pray standing. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he prostrates, prostrate. When he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.’”

The people of Kufah complained about Sa‘d to ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, so he removed him and appointed ‘Ammar over them. Their complaints went so far as to say that he did not know how to pray properly. He sent for him and said, “Abu Ishaq, these people claim that you do not know how to pray properly.” Abu Ishaq said, “As for me, by Allah, I used to lead them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without falling short of it. I would pray the night prayer, taking my time in the first two rak‘ahs and making the last two brief.” He said, “That is what we thought of you, Abu Ishaq.” He sent a man—or men—with him to Kufah, and asked the people of Kufah about him. He left no mosque without asking about him, and they spoke well of him, until he entered a mosque of Banu ‘Abs. A man among them called Usamah ibn Qatadah, known as Abu Sa‘dah, stood and said, “Since you have asked us under oath, Sa‘d does not go out with the military expedition, does not divide equally, and does not judge justly.” Sa‘d said, “By Allah, I will pray for three things: O Allah, if this servant of Yours is lying and stood up to show off and seek reputation, prolong his life, prolong his poverty, and expose him to trials.” Afterwards, when he was asked, he would say, “An old man afflicted with trials; Sa‘d’s prayer has struck me.”
‘Abd al-Malik said: I saw him afterwards, when his eyebrows had fallen over his eyes from old age. He would accost young girls in the streets and pinch them.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque. A man entered and prayed, then greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He returned the greeting and said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed.” He went back and prayed as he had prayed before. Then he came and greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed”—three times. He said, “By the One who sent you with the truth, I know no better than this, so teach me.” He said, “When you stand for prayer, say the takbir, then recite whatever is easy for you of the Quran. Then bow until you are at rest while bowing. Then rise until you stand upright. Then prostrate until you are at rest while prostrating. Then rise until you are at rest while sitting. Do that throughout your prayer.”

english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz. The devils had been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars had been sent against them. The devils returned to their people, who said, “What is the matter with you?” They said, “We have been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us.” They said, “Nothing has come between you and the news of heaven except something that has happened. Travel to the eastern and western parts of the earth, and see what it is that has come between you and the news of heaven.” Those who headed towards Tihamah came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was at Nakhlah, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz, and was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Quran, they listened to it and said, “By Allah, this is what has come between you and the news of heaven.” Then, when they returned to their people, they said, “Our people, ‘We have heard a wondrous Quran, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.’” Allah then revealed to His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Say: It has been revealed to me.”

english_blocks: ‘Ubaydullah said, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

A man of the Ansar used to lead them in prayer in the mosque of Quba’. Whenever he began a surah to recite for them during the prayer, he began with “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” until he finished it, then recited another surah with it. He did this in every rak‘ah. His companions spoke to him, saying, “You begin with this surah, then you do not consider it sufficient until you recite another. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they told him what had happened. He used to lead them in prayer, saying the takbir whenever he lowered himself or rose. When he finished, he said, “My prayer resembles the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more closely than that of any of you.”

arabic_blocks: [753] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد عن غيلان بن جرير عن مطرف بن عبد الله قال صليت خلف علي بن أبي طالب رضى الله تعالى عنه أنا وعمران بن حصين فكان إذا سجد كبر وإذا رفع رأسه كبر وإذا نهض من الركعتين كبر فلما قضى الصلاة أخذ بيدي عمران بن حصين، فقال قد ذكرني هذا صلاة محمد ﷺ أو قال لقد صلى بنا صلاة محمد ﷺ
english_blocks: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Mutarrif ibn ‘Abdullah, who said:

‘Imran ibn Husayn and I prayed behind ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When he prostrated, he said the takbir; when he raised his head, he said the takbir; and when he rose after the two rak‘ahs, he said the takbir. When he finished the prayer, ‘Imran ibn Husayn took my hand and said, “This has reminded me of the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace”—or he said, “He has led us in the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

arabic_blocks: [754] حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال: حدثنا هشيم عن أبي بشر عن عكرمة قال: رأيت رجلا عند المقام يكبر في كل خفض ورفع وإذا قام وإذا وضع فأخبرت بن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال أو ليس تلك صلاة النبي ﷺ لا أم لك
english_blocks: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

I saw a man at the Maqam saying the takbir at every lowering and rising, when he stood and when he lowered himself. I informed Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. He said, “Is that not the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? May you have no mother!”

arabic_blocks: [755] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: أخبرنا همام عن قتادة عن عكرمة قال صليت خلف شيخ بمكة فكبر ثنتين وعشرين تكبيرة فقلت لابن عباس إنه أحمق، فقال ثكلتك أمك سنة أبي القاسم ﷺ، وقال موسى حدثنا أبان حدثنا قتادة حدثنا عكرمة
english_blocks: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam informed us, from Qatadah, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

I prayed behind an old man in Makkah, and he said the takbir twenty-two times. I said to Ibn ‘Abbas, “He is foolish.” He said, “May your mother be bereaved of you! The practice of Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
Musa said: Aban related to us. Qatadah related to us. ‘Ikrimah related to us.

arabic_blocks: [756] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني أبو بكر ابن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث أنه سمع أبا هريرة يقول كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا قام إلى الصلاة يكبر حين يقوم ثم يكبر حين يركع ثم يقول سمع الله لمن حمده حين يرفع صلبه من الركعة ثم يقول وهو قائم ربنا لك الحمد قال عبد الله ولك الحمد ثم يكبر حين يهوي ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه ثم يكبر حين يسجد ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه ثم يفعل ذلك في الصلاة كلها حتى يقضيها ويكبر حين يقوم من الثنتين بعد الجلوس
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah say:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood for prayer, he would say the takbir as he stood, then say the takbir as he bowed. Then he would say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” as he raised his back from bowing. Then, while standing, he would say, “Our Lord, to You belongs praise.”
‘Abdullah said: “And to You belongs praise.”

Then he would say the takbir as he went down, then say the takbir as he raised his head, then say the takbir as he prostrated, then say the takbir as he raised his head. He would then do this throughout the prayer until he completed it. He would say the takbir when he stood after the two rak‘ahs, after sitting.

arabic_blocks: [757] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي يعفور قال: سمعت مصعب بن سعد يقول صليت إلى جنب أبي فطبقت بين كفي ثم وضعتهما بين فخذي فنهاني أبي، وقال كنا نفعله فنهينا عنه وأمرنا أن نضع أيدينا على الركب
english_blocks: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ya‘fur, who said: I heard Mus‘ab ibn Sa‘d say:

I prayed beside my father, pressed my palms together, then put them between my thighs. My father forbade me and said, “We used to do it, then we were forbidden to do it and commanded to put our hands on our knees.”

english_blocks: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb say:

Hudhayfah saw a man who did not complete the bowing and prostration. He said, “You have not prayed. If you were to die, you would die upon something other than the natural disposition with which Allah created Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
